text: chip != desk on frames 427-630 (the henshin stage): the story and the wire both differed. The undefined-behaviour sanitizer: index 575 into a 256-entry palette. The wand's star carried hue_ph >> 9 (up to 127) unmasked, so hue << 4 ran past the table; the chip and the desk found different memory there. Every hue is masked to 15 where it indexes a palette. Same class as THE FISH AFFECT's off-glass run: a reading left its table

C3 cost, first measure: tunnel 64 ms, madness 88 ms, speed lines 37 ms a frame. Everything about a tunnel dot but its heading depends only on its distance, so it became per-distance tables each frame (256 x 16 colours; the face lining 256 x 64): one add and one look-up a dot. Loops walk pointers (no multiply a dot). The face asks only dots that can be on it. The colour split moves two dots a word; the flash is one OR a word; the impact frame a 256-entry table on the wire's low byte; the glitch shifts by even dots so whole words move; the madness tunnel folds its heading through a mirror table (a kaleidoscope for one look-up) and one row serves two. Result over 4 loops: every stage's average at or under 31.7 ms (the wire is 30.7), worst frame 39.0 ms
the float check matched f-mnemonics in the hex column (fadd53e3 is a branch's encoding). It now reads the mnemonic column only. The fish's check had the same pattern and was lucky

the user's panel showed the potato blue: red and blue swapped. The C3 mouth (from HIGH NOON) set MADCTL's BGR bit by default with the comment 'as this panel is'; it never was. Every C3 sketch since HIGH NOON has likely shown swapped colours on this board (HIGH NOON's western palette survives the swap, which is why nobody saw it). Default now RGB; BGR_ORDER flips it back. Pattern: a comment that states a fact about hardware is a claim, not a witness

'screen tearing from loop 1 on': my glitch (random row shifts) leaked into every stage from loop 1 and read exactly as panel tearing. Outside madness it is now a smooth wave; madness's torn rows are tinted magenta or cyan so they read as a glitch. If a moving seam remains, that is the panel's own refresh racing the wire (no TE pin wired)
